Owner(s).note: A Volkswagen Group press release says VW Kraftwerk GmbH is a wholly owned subsidiary of Volkswagen AG and runs the power stations at Wolfsburg. The regulator's list dated 26 June 2026 also names VW Kraftwerk GmbH as the operator of the Wolfsburg gas units. The release does not say in so many words that the company owns the plant, so this is medium.

Captive industry use.note: The Volkswagen Group press release says the Wolfsburg power stations supply most of the power for Volkswagen plants, and supply heat to the Wolfsburg plant and to the city of Wolfsburg. That fits a plant serving both an industrial site and non-industry users. The release does not use the words in GEM's fields, so this is medium.

Captive industry type.note: The press release says the power goes to Volkswagen car and commercial vehicle plants and component plants.

Captive non-industry use.note: The press release says the stations also supply heat to the city of Wolfsburg. It does not say whether that heat is district heating or power, so the existing value is kept.

qa.note: The regulator's list dated 26 June 2026 shows two combined cycle units named GT 31 and GT32 GuD Süd Wolfsburg at 49.4 MW net each, built in 2021 and fed fully into the grid. GEM's West units are 144 MW each. They look like different plants. I did not find a register row for the West units under VW Kraftwerk GmbH.
